title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: PLAC — retain justice ≠ age in sin; not medium
pass_a_gloss: But that reply, which was the second of his, wraps itself in contradiction. For how could Adam, retaining original righteousness, which without doubt is opposed to unrighteousness or sin, grow old in sin, remain turned away from God, a deserter of God, rebellious toward God? For what was that righteousness, except conversion of the heart to God, habitual obedience to God's commands, a constant will of obeying God, and of rendering him his due, by which, by this very thing that it was in him, Adam was righteous? Who then would believe it would have been, that Adam, unless he lost righteousness, would grow old in sin? For on the contrary he would have grown old in righteousness, if indeed he had not lost righteousness. This reply also shows itself ridiculous, when it feigns that righteousness was taken from Adam so that by repenting he might return to God. For so far is it that spiritual death is a means to repentance and conversion to God, that it renders that impossible for the man, and leads him very far away from God. It also seems ridiculous to me, that it is said the sense of that present punishment pricked Adam.
pass_b_english: His second point wraps itself in contradiction. How could Adam, still keeping original righteousness—which is the opposite of unrighteousness and sin—grow old in sin, stay turned from God, desert God, rebel against God? What was that righteousness but a heart turned to God, habitual obedience to his commands, a steady will to obey him and give him his due—the very thing that made Adam righteous while it was in him? Who believes Adam would have grown old in sin unless he had lost righteousness? He would have grown old in righteousness if he had kept it.

The reply also turns silly when it pretends righteousness was stripped from Adam so he might repent and return to God. Spiritual death is so far from being a path to repentance and conversion that it makes them impossible and drives the man farthest from God. And it is silly to say the 'sense' of that present penalty pricked Adam.
source_text: Ea autem, quod secundum erat eius peccatum, sese contradictione involvit. Nam qui potuisset Adamus retinens justitiam originalem, quae sine dubio injustitiae seu peccato opponitur, consenescere in peccato, manere a Deo aversus, Dei desertor, Deo rebellis? Quid enim erat justitia illa, nisi conversio cordis ad Deum, obedientia habitualis Dei mandatis, constans voluntas obediendi Deo, jusque illi suum tribuendi, qua, hoc ipso quod ipsi inerat, justus erat Adamus? Quis ergo futurum fuisse credat, ut Adamus, nisi amitteret justitiam, consenesceret in peccato? Contra enim consensisset in justitia, si quidem justitiam non amisisset. Se quoque ridiculam praebet haec responsio, cum fingit ablatam fuisse Adamo justitiam, ut ad Deum resipiscendo rediret. Tantum enim abest, ut mors spiritualis medium sit ad resipiscentiam, & conversionem ad Deum, ut eam homini reddat impossibilem, eumque a Deo longissime abducat. Ridiculum etiam mihi videtur, quod dicitur, pupugisse Adamum praesentis illius poenae sensum.

choices.choice: cannot keep justice and age in sin; spiritual death not means to repent
